messages.subject: MRDS: never detected objects error
parts:
From: Ainars Aunins [mailto:ainars...@lu.lv]
Sent: Tuesday, July 15, 2014 3:48 PM
To: 'distance-sampling'
Subject: FW: MRDS: never detected objects error

 

Now posting to the correct mailing list hopefully:

 

Dear colleagues,

 

When trying to run MRDS analysis (double observers, „io” type of MR model) I get a following error:

Error in process.data(data, meta.data) :

  following objects were never detected:909

Calls: ddf -> ddf.io -> process.data

Execution halted

As I understand, the message tries to tell me that there are no detections for the object 909 in the data. So I checked the data and did not find any error – one of the observers has detected it  (the 2nd observer has „1” for „detected” while the 1st observer „0” for detected). And there are only 2 lines for the object 909, no more lines with this object.

I also ran the analysis in debug mode and checked the data file “ddf.dat.r” generated by Distance in the temp folder – still found no errors for the object 909.

What could be wrong? Am I misunderstanding the error message?

 

Best wishes

Ainars Aunins

messages.author: 0ec6e2b452a0c672
messages.subject: Re: MRDS: never detected objects error
parts:
Ainars-

The code assumes that the observations are ordered (object x observer 1, object x observer 2, object y observer 1, object y observer 2 etc or (object x observer 1, object y observer 1, object x observer 2, object y observer 2 etc) and objects 895 and 894 are intermingled with other objects for the 2 observers which is causing the code to issue an erroneous message. I thought the code in the Distance interface ordered them but apparently not. I'll add a line of R code to order them in the next version of the package but in the meantime, if you fix those lines it should work fine except that you can't use variables like seat and expert in the dsmodel formula. When I reordered the records and ran your model it threw an error that you used a factor with only one level - which was seat because it only had one value for observer==1. The distance sampling detection function is for the pooled observations - seen by at least one observer.  You can use seat and expert in the mrmodel.  Observer type measures for the distance sampling detection function can only be done in pairs (ie a pair of experts vs a pair of non-experts) because the pairs of data are treated as a unit in the distance sampling detection function.

--jeff

messages.author: 3cc57783657c133b
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Re: MRDS: never detected objects error
parts:
With the kind help of Eric Rexstad the problem was solved off-list.
The problem was caused by 2 objects (none of them was listed among those in the error message), where the primary and secondary observers did not agree on the species they had observed. So there were different names in the species field of the database for these objects. Using a query in the Distance program the records not matching the right species name were not included in the dataset sent to R. This caused mismatch in the observations/detections by the two observers.
Just a suggestion to the developers of the 'mrds' package: it would be nice if a data checking routine could be included in the code that would check for such cases and list the right object IDs in the error message.

best wishes
Ainars Aunins
